root_cause.classification: A) submit_work exposed a non-canonical task_type value
root_cause.evidence: 'engineering' has never been a registered task_type in registry_data/capabilities.json (52 real distinct task_types exist across the full registry; the closest real one is 'code_edit'). evolution/advance.py._implementation_router() hardcodes studio_router.rank("code_edit", ...) as the ONLY task_type it ever routes to at real execution time, regardless of what task_type a proposal recorded -- confirmed by direct grep, not inference. submit_work had zero validation/normalization of its caller-supplied task_type string against the real registry, so a natural Founder-facing label like 'engineering' silently produced a correct-but-unhelpful default-deny (0 registered candidates for a string nothing claims), even though a perfectly good real route existed under its actual name.
root_cause.not_the_cause: authority_policy, resource policy, capability registration, and the router's scoring/duty-cycle logic were all already correct and unmodified -- verified by re-running the prior campaign's canary (c8a014b5) through the real timer: it reached promotion_candidate with selected_engine=omni_engineer, provider=ollama, confirming the resource-policy hard filter and duty-cycle-among-eligible-candidates logic both work exactly as designed. The only broken layer was external-facing task_type naming.

fix.scope: services/th3_mcp/tools.py and mcp_core.py ONLY -- zero changes to studio_router.py, evolution/advance.py, evolution/proposal.py, capability_registry.py, or authority_policy.py this campaign. No new task_type was registered, no worker capability was registered for anything it can't do, no protected gate was touched.
fix.mechanism: _normalize_task_type(): a short, explicit alias table (engineering/engineer/software_engineering/coding/code/development/dev/implementation -> code_edit) applied at the top of both submit_work and route_preview, before any rank()/classification call. Anything NOT in this explicit list passes through completely unchanged, so the existing default-deny behavior for genuinely unroutable task_type values is untouched -- verified live with task_type='quantum_computing' still producing capability_gap=true.
fix.transparency: Both tools now report task_type_submitted (the caller's original string) and task_type (the normalized value actually used for routing) plus task_type_was_normalized, so nothing is silently substituted without the caller being able to see it.
